shot.prose: The board reads clean at this width: task cards line up in a tidy three-column grid with consistent gutters, and the active-task strip at the top is the clearest visual anchor on the page. The status dot on each card is doing real work — green/amber/grey reads instantly — but the landed cards below fade to the same grey as the dormant ones, so a shipped task and an idea look identical at a glance. The usage rail on the right is a bit lonely: two thin bars in a lot of empty vertical space that the eye keeps sliding past.

findings.what: landed and idea cards share one grey
usage rail has roughly 40% empty space below its two meters
active strip and the board below share no visual separation

shot.prose: Three even columns, a legible status dot, and a clear top strip for what's running now — the bones are right. Two things read as unfinished rather than intentional: the landed section directly beneath dormant cards uses identical typography and colour, so 'done' looks like 'not started yet'; and the usage rail's two meters sit at the top of a column that runs another 300-400px past them with nothing in it, which reads as a sidebar built for more content than currently exists. Neither breaks the page, but both cost it a beat of confidence on first look.

findings.what: landed cards read identical to dormant ones
usage rail column runs well past its own content

shot.prose: At 3440 the three-column grid stays exactly three columns and does not add a fourth, so the whole right half of the screen is a flat, empty gutter with nothing in it — the layout picked a card width and stopped scaling. The usage rail on the far right is now stranded a full screen-width from the cards it relates to, which breaks the reading relationship that worked at 1280. Nothing here is broken in the sense of overlap or clipping; it is simply a layout that never decided what to do with the space it was given.

findings.what: grid stays 3 columns at 3440, leaving roughly half the width empty
usage rail sits a full screen away from the cards it relates to

shot.prose: Cropped to just the board: the card grid itself is tidy — even gutters, consistent card height, a status dot that reads at a glance. Isolated like this nothing looks wrong, which is worth noting on its own: the problems this shot doesn't show (the empty usage rail, the flat landed/dormant grey) are context problems, not card problems. This region is doing its job.

A dense but organised measuring page: the code sample, the finding census and the live re-run block move top to bottom in a sensible order, and the monospace metric blocks give the eye a clear place to land. The one thing that reads slightly off is the census — four rows of prose-length findings with no visual weight difference between a severe one and a minor one, so the page asks you to read every line to know which matters.

findings.what: findings list has no severity weight beyond a small label

shot.prose: The page keeps its column bounded rather than stretching the prose edge to edge, which is the right call at this width — nothing here reads as sprawl. The metric blocks do widen into a longer row, which is fine, but the finding census below them stays a single narrow column beside a large flat gutter on the right; a second column of findings would use that space instead of leaving it as margin.

findings.what: finding census stays single-column beside a wide empty gutter
